text: Then suddenly, as he rested there, the room was filled with the strong, sweet odor of mignonette, a scent so clear that it seemed almost like a living visitor. <break time="0.8s" /> What, dear, he cried aloud, as if someone had called to him, and he sprang up and turned around to see who was there. <break time="0.8s" /> It was the scent that she had loved and made her own, and he was certain that she had been in this very room not long before. <break time="0.8s" /> In the dresser and drawers he found hairpins, a worn handkerchief smelling of heliotrope, buttons, and a theater program, but none of them could tell him about her. <break time="0.8s" /> He held a black satin hair bow for a long moment, but it too was a common thing, an ordinary ornament that told no tales about its owner. <break time="0.8s" /> He crawled over the floor and searched every corner, calling Yes, dear, to the empty air, but he found nothing except old corks and cigarettes. <break time="0.8s" /> He hurried down to the housekeeper and begged her to tell him who had lived in the room before he came. <break time="0.8s" /> Miss Sprowls and Missus Mooney left a week ago Tuesday, she answered, describing a short, stout woman with black hair, and then she named other tenants from long before.
